blocks.x: Streaming platforms live on two curves: engagement (personalization, discovery, retention) and unit economics (encoding, delivery, churn). Both are decision engines, and both run better on governed telemetry, evaluation-driven ML and cost telemetry. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in personalization/discovery, subscriber lifecycle, delivery cost management, with experimentation close behind. Volume grows on every path; the decision layer has not kept up. That gap is measurable, and it is the work.
Streaming & Digital Platforms: the queues and waits that come up first,

items: Recommendations plateau without governance over objectives (engagement vs. satisfaction).
View definitions, session metrics and retention measures inconsistent; product decisions wobble.
Cost per stream/hour by CDN/region/codec unknown; margin leaks.
Password sharing and stream-ripping drain ARPU; enforcement blunt.
Cancellation intents handled at save-desk; churn prediction un-wired to actions.
Experiment platform bottlenecks; product teams queue.
